prompt: The evaluation repository asks the agent to "Apply threat model expertise to this task". The fixture contains a plausible happy path, an adjacent-skill decoy, one invalid or partial state, and a recovery-sensitive path that must be modeled and handed to verification rather than assumed. The acceptance boundary is threat-modeling-practice: Define scope and security objectives, then map assets, actors, identities, data/control flows, trust boundaries, dependencies, entry points, privilege transitions, and recovery paths. The adjacent application-security discipline is a routing decoy unless its separate responsibility is actually requested. Resolve environment facts that change the answer, preserve existing contracts and user-owned state, and produce prioritized abuse/control mappings plus reproducible success, negative-path, and recovery verification cases with execution status explicit. Do not invent executed proof when the fixture provides design evidence only.

requirements: architecture/data-flow fixture covering API, identity context, queue, worker, storage, signed URLs, webhooks, support administration, and disaster recovery
stated product security objectives plus explicit non-goals and known assumptions
actor/identity inventory including ordinary tenant user, compromised tenant user, service identity, support operator, and external webhook endpoint
asynchronous retry and restore-path evidence that can expose stale authorization or resurrected state
representative negative, interruption, compatibility, or recovery path

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The result must establish the actual threat-modeling-practice boundary and relevant environment before acting, preserve the hierarchy relationship (near-neighbor=application-security), and not absorb the near-neighbor responsibility merely because it is adjacent.
Define scope and security objectives, then map assets, actors, identities, data/control flows, trust boundaries, dependencies, entry points, privilege transitions, and recovery paths.
The result must make its consequential assumptions, ownership, and decision sequence explicit and reproducible.

Trace top threats to observed or planned enforcing layers, define concrete success/negative/recovery verification cases and owners, label execution status, revisit the model after architecture/identity changes, and record residual risk and assumptions explicitly.

The result must not take the tempting shortcut prohibited by this skill: Do not produce diagram-only threat models, enumerate theoretical threats without prioritization, treat prompts/UI as enforcement, or claim a mitigation exists without locating its enforcing layer.

Every material completion claim must map to observable evidence (System, identity, data/control-flow, and trust-boundary model; Attacker capabilities, assumptions, and prioritized abuse cases; Mitigation-to-enforcement and residual-risk map; Verification priorities without unsupported executed-proof claims), with simulated, unavailable, inferred, stale, or unresolved evidence labeled rather than converted into certainty.
